subject: green sea slug
title: This Animal Steals Its Food Factory From Plants

scenes.text: This animal eats algae, and steals its sunlight power.
It's a sea slug called Elysia chlorotica, only about as long as a postage stamp.
It sucks the green chloroplasts out of the algae it eats. Most slugs just digest them.
This one keeps them inside its body, and they keep working for months.
Kept in good light, it can live for months without eating again.
Scientists even reported an algae gene in the slug that helps repair them. An animal running on stolen solar panels.

description:
This animal eats algae and steals its sunlight power.
The sea slug Elysia chlorotica keeps stolen chloroplasts in its gut, where they keep working for months.
Would you want to photosynthesize?
first_comment: Part animal, part solar panel. What other animal should we ask: how does it even do that?
